goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.java:213 — When a client-specific resource exists only that resource is evaluated and the 'all Clients' resource is ignored, so an admin with MANAGE on all clients is denied for a client whose own resource carries a different scope, contradicting the interface javadoc

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the code first looks up a per-client Resource by name = client.getId(). Only if that lookup returns null does it fall back to the resource-type (“all clients”) resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Therefore, when a client-specific resource exists, permissions granted on the “all clients” resource are never evaluated. This contradicts the interface/javadoc expectation for V2 methods (e.g., canManage(ClientModel)) that global permissions on all clients (AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE/VIEW/etc.) should also grant access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.java:84-86 — canView() (and thus canViewClientScopes()/canList()) checks only the VIEW scope while canView(ClientScopeModel) accepts VIEW or MANAGE; an admin with MANAGE on all clients passes canManage() but fails requireView()/requireViewClientScopes() on realm-level list endpoints, inconsistent with javadoc and V1 manage-implies-view semantics

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2, realm-level `canView()` is implemented as `return canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW);` and does not consider `MANAGE` permissions. Meanwhile `canView(ClientScopeModel)` explicitly allows either `VIEW` or `MANAGE` (`return hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE)`). Since `canList()`/`canViewClientScopes()` are documented to be based on `canView()`, an admin granted only the `MANAGE` scope on the global "Clients" resource would be allowed by `canManage()` but would still fail realm-level view/list checks that rely on `canView()`. This is an observable inconsistency introduced in the diff and breaks the common manage-implies-view expectation already reflected elsewhere in this same class (e.g., `canView(ClientModel)` allows via `canConfigure` -> `canManage`).
